page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category, with single-threaded gzip compression rated as poor. However, multi-core performance is consistently average, as demonstrated by Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth is average for large block reads and writes, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive applications that do not demand high single-threaded compute performance. It is well-suited for workloads such as in-memory caching with Redis, where it achieves an average of 11.3 million operations per second, database operations, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks.
